messages:
sophia: Quick heads-up — ran speculative prefetch + q4f16 bring-up on Llama3-12B (KV-split patch). Median latency down ~32% vs baseline, p99 ~18% lower, but we see a quality hit on long-form summarization (ROUGE-2 drop ~0.9). Dumping quick notes here for visibility.

matt: Nice. Which sampling / decode config did you use? and how many spec windows?

sophia: short version: top-k=50, temp=0.8, greedy fallback for speculative failures, spec windows [1,2,4], prefetch_kv=True, batch=4. Ran on conv_summ and longdoc_summ eval sets.

sophia: command:
```
# local bench command
python bench/spec_prefetch.py \\
  --model llama3-12b-q4f16 \\
  --spec_windows 1,2,4 \\
  --prefetch_kv True \\
  --batch 4 \\
  --sampling topk --k 50 --temp 0.8
```

ankur: thanks — can you paste the small eval table? rough numbers are fine.

sophia: sure. quick table (median latency / ROUGE-2):
- baseline (no spec, q4f16): 210ms median / 18.4
- spec-prefetch (1,2,4): 142ms median / 17.5
- relative: -32% latency, -0.9 ROUGE-2

leo: interesting. is the quality regression concentrated in specific prompts or across the board?

sophia: looks concentrated: longdoc_summ with >3k tokens context. Shorter convo summarization is fine, sometimes slightly better (noise). For long docs the model starts producing fluffier endings and loses some entity fidelity.

eval-bot: auto-eval summary: throughput 630 tok/s (single A100 v4 sim), p95 latency 290ms, failure cases flagged: 42/500 examples with missing citations, 18/500 with repeated sentence fragments. Full CSV uploaded to: https://redwood.internal/evals/1875001234.csv

matt: possible hypotheses: (1) spec-prefetch generates token predictions that bias KV cache and make subsequent autoregression conditioned on slightly wrong keys, (2) quantization magnifies small logits differences so prefetch errors are stickier.

ankur: agree. we should run two ablations: (A) spec-prefetch off but keep same decode parallelism, (B) prefetched KV but force deterministic re-eval of first N tokens (i.e., re-roll cache). Also try lower temp for prefetch stage (0.2) to reduce variance.

sophia: already started A/B: when prefetch disabled but runtime batching kept, latency improvement collapses to ~8% (so the big wins are from prefetch path). For B (re-roll first 2 tokens) latency saves ~24% and ROUGE-2 drop reduces to ~0.3.

leo: promising — sounds like a small revalidation window helps. Can we automate a policy: re-roll first 2 tokens for docs > 2k tokens?

sophia: yes we can add heuristic in runtime: if context_len > 2048 then revalidate first 2 prefetched tokens. Cheap to implement.

ankur: also let's run a human evaluation (n=200) focused on factual consistency for long docs. auto ROUGE may miss hallucinated facts.

sophia: adding to queue. I’ll kick off a 2k-run with two temps (0.2/0.8) and re-roll=0/2 to collect both automatic metrics and a human pass/fail. Expected runtime ~6h.

matt: ping me when results land. can we also try q8_0 (higher-bit) to isolate quantization effect?

sophia: good call — will add q8_0 run.

eval-bot: note: budgeted runs for this experiment are in project "spec-prefetch-2026". Cost estimate ~ $180 for full ablation sweep.

leo: next steps checklist: 1) run re-roll ablation + temps + q8_0 (sophia) 2) human eval (ankur + crowd) 3) implement runtime heuristic if ablation confirms improvement (leo) 4) document regression cases and file a postmortem if needed (matt).

sophia: adding GH issue: https://redwood.internal/gh/spec-prefetch/issues/291 — will attach CSV and sample failure prompts.

ankur: :eyes: nice thread. small ask — include a couple of raw examples in the issue (one good, one bad) so we can inspect decode traces / kv differences.

sophia: will add. thanks all.
